title: Cheep-Cheep! The Chicks' Little Ladder
summary: In Rabbi Yosef's yard stands a little wooden ladder that the chicks climb to drink water. But to honor an important guest, the whole house is cleaned, and the ladder disappears into the shed! The chicks jump, fall and cheep: we need a drink! Who will hear them? And what will be waiting on the doorstep in the morning? A rhyming story about kindness to small animals, based on a tale from Kav HaYashar.
pages:
In Rabbi Yosef's yard, by the coop and the garden so green,
stood a little wooden ladder, the narrowest you've seen.
Little chicks climbed it, tip-top, up to the top,
to drink clear water from the blue bowl, every drop.

One day a guest came by, a wise rabbi with a beard so white,
and Rabbi Yosef was happy: "Welcome! Sit and rest, it's all right!"
And Rivka called out: "A guest? Everyone clean, quick, quick, let's go!
We'll sweep and we'll scrub until everything's aglow!"

And Tova swept: shhh-shhh, and scrubbed till it all shone bright,
and suddenly she saw the ladder: "What's this doing here, standing in my way, not right?"
She lifted it up, hop!, and carried it away from that spot,
into the dark shed, by the old bucket and pot.

The chicks came to drink — hop! — but wait, what is this?
No ladder, no step, just a wall high as this!
They jumped and they fell — plop, plop! — ten little balls, down they sink:
Cheep-cheep, cheep-cheep! We need a drink!

They stood on each other, a tower of yellow feathers stacked with care,
and the tower wobbled... and fell! Plop! Like a pile of cakes, everywhere.
And Mother Hen ran around, cluck-cluck!, watching her little ones, too worried to blink:
Cheep-cheep, cheep-cheep! We need a drink!

And the cheeping rose higher and higher, over the roof, over the garden, so high,
and the wise guest lifted his head from his old book, wondering why.
He listened... and listened... and heard, as if from the sky's very brink:
Cheep-cheep, cheep-cheep! We need a drink!

"Rabbi Yosef," said the guest, "your house shines like a diamond's gleam,
but where is the little ladder that stood here till today, it would seem?"
Rabbi Yosef searched in the closet, under the bed, and in every corner and nook,
and in the shed, by the bucket... there it is! The ladder! Look!

Rabbi Yosef ran and put the ladder back in its place,
and the chicks climbed up, tip-top!, like a dream, with a smile on each face.
They drank and they drank, glug-glug!, cool, good water, quick as a wink:
Cheep-cheep, cheep-cheep! We've had our drink!

Mother Hen bowed her head: cluck-cluck, cluck-cluck, thank you so much!
And Tova patted the ladder: "From now on you stay here, by the bowl, and nobody will touch!"
And the chicks stood on the rungs, in a row, like a choir in a line,
and sang a thank-you song to the whole house, with a clear voice and joy so fine.

And in the morning, on the doorstep, a white egg... crack! The newest, tiniest chick ever seen!
And the ladder? It stands in the yard, by the coop and the garden so green.
And the chick climbed up, tip-top!, and drank and drank, with a happy wink:
Cheep-cheep, cheep-cheep! We've had our drink!
